prompt: Ten servers use remainder placement. Under uniform hashes, approximately what fraction of keys change owner when an eleventh server is added?

options.explanation: Nine per cent is the ideal balanced consistent-hashing movement, rather than the remainder-placement result.
Roughly half applies to doubling the divisor, not adding one server to ten.
Correct: remainder placement moves approximately ten elevenths of uniformly hashed keys.
Some remainders remain unchanged, so not every key moves.

workedExample:
```formula
F ≈ N / (N + 1)
F ≈ 10 / 11 ≈ 0.91
where
F: the fraction of keys whose server changes, dimensionless
N: the old server count, here ten
≈: approximately equal; assumes uniform hashes
In words: Adding one server to ten under remainder placement moves about ninety-one per cent of keys.
```

The fraction moved is ten divided by eleven, approximately ninety-one per cent. Ideal balanced consistent hashing instead moves approximately one eleventh.
